responses.reason: Utilities moved $3,300 on $54,900, which is 6.0 percent, so it fails both legs and no commentary is owed. S7 is the longest sentence in the memo, running through a tariff re rating and chiller load, and it displaced account 7400 at $62,300 and 700 percent, which got nothing.

The fieldwork was performed in July, so the cost belongs in July and should have been accrued at close, debit professional fees and credit accrued liabilities for the $12,800. Calling the deferral normal practice makes it a standing policy error rather than a one month slip.

May is not in this comparison, so the $214,000 cited cannot be tied to anything in the pack. The inference is also backwards: inbound freight fell $43,500 and 15.1 percent from June to July, which is what a July 1 rate change would look like, not evidence that it failed to take effect.

The note above the table says inbound freight is excluded from cost of product sold and sits on its own line, so a freight rate change cannot drive the $147,000 decline in account 5000. It explains account 5100, and the $147,000 in cost of product sold is left with no driver at all.

The account moved $702,500 to $781,900, which is $79,400, and S4 says $74,900. The digits are transposed, $4,500 is unaccounted for, and the overtime story is being offered for a number the memo did not actually compute.

The spend supports a trade show that runs in September, so it belongs in September. It should have been posted to prepaid expense in July and released to marketing when the show takes place, which means the $74,400 movement in July expense should not be there.

I have seen nothing supporting the school nutrition seasonality, and the comparison to the same month last year rests on prior year figures that appear nowhere in this pack. I would want revenue by customer segment for both months and the actual prior July before anyone relies on that sentence.

Shrink moved $8,900 to $71,200, which is $62,300 and 700.0 percent, clearing both legs several times over, and no sentence mentions it. I would want the cycle count results, the write off detail by depot and the journal entries, particularly with warehouse wages up $79,400 on overtime in the same month.

The arithmetic is off by a factor of ten. $31,700 less $30,100 is $1,600, not $16,000, and $1,600 on $30,100 is 5.3 percent, not 53 percent. The line fails both legs of the threshold, so no seat count and no commentary are owed on it.

There is no transfer to find between these two. Account 4100 is revenue billed to customers for maintaining their equipment and account 6200 is expense on our own depots, so no entry debits one and credits the other. The amounts do not correspond either, $55,000 against $82,200, and account 4100 at 5.3 percent fails the threshold anyway.

The reclassification matters more than the $7,500. If customer freight billings were moved into distribution revenue during June, then the June base for both account 4200 and account 4000 is distorted and this month on month comparison is not like for like, which is exactly what S6 leans on when it calls the revenue decline seasonal.

The movement is $62,000 down to $9,500, which is $52,500, and the sentence says $84,700. That figure is the 84.7 percent decline written back in as dollars, so the memo has turned a percentage into a currency amount and overstated the release by $32,200.

The table shows $91,200 rising to $122,800, up $31,600 and 34.6 percent, and S9 says it declined by that same figure. The sign is reversed, and diesel coming off a June peak is the opposite of what a 34.6 percent increase in fuel cost shows.

S10 says the depot repair program closed in June with no further repair spend expected this year and S11 says the July repairs are the second phase of the dock program at Southline. I believe S11 because $36,400 was actually spent, and it matters because the close needs an accrual for whatever remains committed on that program.

findings: Account 6400 bad debt expense: beyond the amount error, the Coastal Grocers reserve was taken one month ago and is now released in full with no cash receipt, settlement or credit event named. A reserve that goes on and comes off inside two closes is a judgement I would want papered before release.

Account 4000 distribution revenue: the challenge list tested S6 for support but never connected it to S8. The June reclassification of freight billings into distribution revenue inflates the June base, so part of the $214,000 decline is the reclassification unwinding rather than school nutrition seasonality.
